solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Boast about visiting great eccentric old star

indicators.note: visiting means calling in on, so the turned-round boast goes inside the other pieces
eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters of great are rearranged
about says the word for boast is turned round

parts.note: to boast is to brag

explanation.surface: A braggart turns up at the home of some bizarre faded celebrity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visiting' looks like mere company, but the boast goes in between the rearranged great and the O. 'star' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbo was a Swedish-born Hollywood screen legend of the 1920s and 30s, a famous film actress.

clue.text: Leave a large target

parts.note: to leave is to go
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: An instruction to abandon an ambitious aim.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal is an aim or objective, something you set your sights on.

clue.text: Eat out along with others at hotel

parts.note: etc, et cetera, means 'and the rest'
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A suggestion to dine out in company at a hotel restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eat out' looks like dining in a restaurant; here it means corrode away, as acid does on a metal plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Etching uses acid to corrode a surface, so to etch is to eat away at it.

clue.text: Automation has largely replaced this rally course

parts.note: a rally is a gathering or assembly of people
a course or route is a line

explanation.surface: Robots now do much of the work at a car-rally route, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Factory production lines, once staffed by workers, are now largely run by robots and machines.

clue.text: A lousy bunch book girl

parts.note: a bunch of lice is literally lousy, infested with lice

explanation.surface: A rude description of a group of people, followed by a girl from a novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's heroine who goes to Wonderland is the best-known girl in a book title.

clue.text: Crazy learner is in sea

indicators.note: in says the learner and 'is' go inside the name of the sea

parts.note: the Baltic is the sea bordered by Scandinavia, Germany and the Baltic states
L is for learner, as on British learner-driver plates

explanation.surface: A novice sailor all at sea goes mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Going ballistic is flying into a rage, so the word is used informally for wildly angry or crazy.

clue.text: Cross most of Iberia without one

indicators.note: without says the letter for one is removed

parts.note: Spain takes up most of the Iberian peninsula, Portugal the rest
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A traveller crosses much of the peninsula alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' suggests cutting a letter off IBERIA; instead it is a definition of Spain, the larger part of the peninsula.
explanation.definitionFit: To span a river is to bridge it, extending across from side to side.

clue.text: Employ both tanks opening vessel

indicators.note: tanks means fails or collapses, so the letters break apart and reform

explanation.surface: An army deploying two armoured vehicles to open up a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tanks' looks like armour but is a verb, collapse, signalling the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlebotomy is the medical practice of cutting open a vein to draw blood; a vein is a blood vessel.

clue.text: My French upset banker securing best alias

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the French word is read backwards

parts.note: mon is French for my

indicators.note: securing means holding something inside it

parts.note: a banker is a river, something with banks; the Dee is a British river
plum means the best, as in a plum job

explanation.surface: A disgruntled bank worker hides the best of something under a false name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banker' is crossword shorthand for a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen name is an assumed name a writer uses, a kind of alias.

clue.text: Handy current local tax authority losing its head

parts.note: AC is alternating current
cess is an old word for a local rate or tax, still used in Ireland and Scotland

indicators.note: losing its head says the first letter of the word for authority is cut off

parts.note: a bible is an authoritative book on a subject

explanation.surface: A council tax office conveniently loses its chief.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'bible' in the sense of an authority, minus its first letter, gives IBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something accessible is easy to reach or use, so convenient and close at hand.

clue.text: One's reluctant to open up seafood

definitions.meaning: someone who will not talk is said to ... up, shutting like a bivalve shell
a bivalve mollusc eaten as shellfish

explanation.surface: A shy diner refuses to crack open their shellfish.
explanation.definitionFit: The shellfish keeps its shell shut tight, hence the idiom for staying silent.

clue.text: Small milliner with soft top withstanding crash

parts.note: a milliner makes hats, so is a hatter
p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
a roof is the top of a building

explanation.surface: A tiny hat-maker with a soft cap survives an accident.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass that resists breaking into pieces on impact can survive a crash intact.

clue.text: One simple herb, a riotous perennial

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: riotous means wild and disorderly, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A modest garden herb runs riot as a plant that comes back every year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perennial' looks like a gardening noun but is the adjective, everlasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Perennial means lasting for ever, enduring year after year without dying out.

clue.text: 3D artwork, a jumble reflecting bold angles oddly

indicators.note: reflecting means mirrored, so the word for jumble is read backwards

parts.note: a jumble is a mess

indicators.note: oddly picks the first, third, fifth and so on letters of the words

explanation.surface: A messy sculpture mirrors strong, angular shapes.
explanation.definitionFit: In art, an assemblage is a three-dimensional collage built from found objects.

clue.text: Engineer hated to check out Beetle

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or rebuild, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: to watch is to keep an eye on or check out

explanation.surface: An engineer who hated the job is told to inspect a Volkswagen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beetle' with its capital suggests the car; it is the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: The deathwatch beetle bores into old timber; its tapping was once taken as an omen of death.

clue.text: Sense something fishy — set alarm off to catch rudd primarily

indicators.note: to catch means to hold something inside, so the rearranged letters take in one more
off means gone wrong or awry, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the setter's slip: the first letter of the fish's name is R, but the answer needs an L here

explanation.surface: An angler grows suspicious when the alarm goes off as a fish bites.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges SET ALARM into SMELARAT, which must catch an L. 'rudd primarily' gives R, not L: a slip by the setter that the blog's commenters also noted.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell a rat is the idiom for suspecting that something is wrong or dishonest.

clue.text: Tough sister, distressed, accepts bronze

indicators.note: accepts means takes in, so one piece holds the other
distressed means damaged or upset, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: tan is a bronze, sun-browned colour

explanation.surface: A hardy sister, upset, still takes a medal for third place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bronze' suggests a third-place medal; it is the colour of a suntan.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tough holds out against force or wear, so it withstands it.

clue.text: Drink a litre outright

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: A command to down a whole litre in one go.
explanation.definitionFit: Total and outright both mean complete and absolute, as in a total or outright failure.

clue.text: Praise group coming from Sussex to Leicester

indicators.note: a group of letters coming from the words that follow is the hidden answer

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A band touring from the south coast to the Midlands earns acclaim.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Praise group' as the definition; 'group' cannot belong there, since the answer is a verb, so it joins 'coming from' as the hiding signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to laud something enthusiastically, a synonym of praise as a verb.

clue.text: Devoted Yankee parent second in game with Mike

indicators.note: in says the word for second sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: soccer is association football
M is Mike in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: An American mother, a second player in a match, alongside someone called Mike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yankee' could be Y in the phonetic alphabet; here it just means American.
explanation.definitionFit: A US suburban mother who devotes her time to driving her children to youth sports is the stereotype.

clue.text: Box office sticks nonsense at end of performance

definitions.text: Box office sticks nonsense at end of performance

parts.note: wands are slender sticks
crap is slang for rubbish or nonsense

indicators.note: end of picks the last letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: The theatre box office talks rubbish once the show is over.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue pictures the obsequious bowing a performer does as the curtain falls.
explanation.definitionFit: To be excessively deferential is to bend low and shuffle back, as courtiers did.

clue.text: Quickly make approach to jumping-off point

definitions.meaning: to put together fast, as with a dress on a sewing machine
the sprint an athlete takes before leaping

explanation.surface: A long-jumper hurries towards the take-off board.
explanation.definitionFit: One phrase means to produce something hastily and the sprint before a jump, two separate idioms.

clue.text: Put it up behind the old snowman

indicators.note: behind says the reversed piece comes after the other

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: An instruction to pile it on top of an old snowman in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman of the Himalayas is the legendary ape-like creature also called by this name.

clue.text: Venison the only dish at this party?

definitions.text: Venison the only dish at this party?

parts.words: Venison the only dish at this party
parts.note: venison is deer meat, and a male deer gives its name to a men-only pre-wedding party

explanation.surface: A dinner guest wonders why only deer is being served.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor party for the groom is named after a male deer, the source of venison.

clue.text: Start off jolly pretentiously cultured

indicators.note: start off says the first letter of the word is removed

parts.note: a jolly is a party or outing

explanation.surface: Kicking off cheerfully in a way that tries too hard to be sophisticated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jolly' reads as an adverb; it is the noun, a party or jaunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes someone affecting an interest in the arts, a showy rather than genuine culture.

clue.text: Data gathered in least common ecosystem

indicators.note: gathered in means taken inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: rarest means least common
info, information, is data

explanation.surface: Researchers collect data on the rarest habitats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical forest with heavy rainfall is a distinct habitat of interacting species, an example of an ecosystem.

clue.text: Copy City head office

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial district

explanation.surface: A bank's headquarters in the City of London imitates others.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo is to repeat or imitate what someone else has said.

clue.text: Sets back furniture initially in studying flooring

indicators.note: back says the word for sets is read in reverse

parts.note: to set something down is to put it

indicators.note: in says the furniture's initial goes inside the other word

parts.note: eying, a variant of eyeing, means looking at closely

indicators.note: initially picks the first letter of furniture

explanation.surface: Someone replaces furniture while studying a new floor covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flooring' looks like floorboards but means knocking flat, astounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Flooring a person figuratively is amazing them, leaving them stunned, which is what stupefying news does.
